title: 5-ALA and respiration
summary: A single precursor may expose a bottleneck in heme production.

graph.evidence: 5-ALA altered electron transfer and ATP in FLVCR1 fibroblasts.
graph.inference: The tested concentration was far above the measured pediatric plasma peak.
graph.hypothesis: Local 5-ALA could restore function if precursor supply limits heme production.
graph.experiment: Measure labelled heme and ATP-linked oxygen use at matched iron and exposure.

evidence: The FLVCR1 experiment used 5,000 µM in culture. The highest measured parent plasma peak in the exploratory Leigh study was 12.3 µM.
inference: The Leigh withdrawal trial tested the iron combination. It recorded loss of efficacy in 2/13 versus 7/14 and did not confirm its primary result.
hypothesis: Precursor supply, downstream conversion and iron can each affect respiration. Accumulating porphyrin would favor a conversion limit.
experiment: Compare labelled heme in respiratory complexes and ATP-linked oxygen use in matched WWOX preparations. Include an iron-only control.
limits: Conditional metabolic comparator. Pediatric WWOX neural exposure and benefit remain unverified.
